result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_edge_attrs_by_id()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get attribute values for edges by edge ID. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L13656-L13740){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_edge_attrs_by_id( edge_attr, edges=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Get edge attributes by id](/assets/graphs/get-edge-attrs-by-id.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared four-node graph with edge ids on the edges; every edge has an attribute w. The queried edges 2 (A to C) and 5 (C to D) are outlined in the accent color with their ids highlighted. The card maps just those two ids to their values: 2 is 4 and 5 is 1." width="100%"} Reads one named attribute from a list of edges identified by their internal edge IDs and returns a dictionary keyed by those IDs. It works like `get_edge_attrs()`, but instead of filtering by endpoint nodes it takes the edge IDs directly, which is convenient when they come from another call such as `find_edge_ids()`, `get_selected_edge_ids()`, or a DataFrame column. The graph is not modified. Edges that don't have the attribute are left out of the result, and IDs that don't exist in the graph are silently skipped, so the dictionary may have fewer entries than the IDs requested. As elsewhere, `"weight"` reads the edge's first-class weight. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The name of the attribute to read (e.g., `"weight"`, `"rel"`). Edges without this attribute are omitted; if none of the queried edges has it, an empty dict is returned. [edges]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A list of edge IDs (`int`) to query. If `None` (the default), all edges are queried, which gives the same result as `get_edge_attrs()` without filters. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, any]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping edge IDs to attribute values. Only includes edges that exist and have the attribute set. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} This keys the lookup on edge ID directly rather than searching by source/target. Here only the first edge is requested: ::: {#b53d7edd .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges( [ ("A", "B", 1.5, {"type": "friend"}), ("B", "C", 2.0, {"type": "colleague"}), ] ) ) edge_ids = graph.get_edge_ids() graph.get_edge_attrs_by_id("weight", edges=edge_ids[:1]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {1: 1.5} ``` ::: ::: Omitting `edges=` queries every edge in the graph: ::: {#acb7e379 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_edge_attrs_by_id("type") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {1: 'friend', 2: 'colleague'} ``` ::: ::: A common pattern is to read attributes for the edges currently selected: ::: {#22bd2076 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.select_edges(lambda e: e.weight is not None and e.weight > 1.8) graph.get_edge_attrs_by_id("type", edges=graph.get_selected_edge_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {2: 'colleague'} ``` ::: :::
